newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller in Jordan for talks with Hussein.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller in Jordan for talks with Hussein.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller arrived in Jordan on Monday for talks with King Hussein on economic development and security cooperation.

"We have come...to benefit our two countries in terms of the economy, in terms of the (Middle East) peace process that Jordan has contributed to in a very extensive way and we want to share our views on security interests in the region as a whole," Ciller told reporters on arrival.
Ciller, who is due to meet the king later on Monday, was met by Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.

Her trip follows talks in Amman on Thursday between Jordanian and Turkish air commanders. Ankara and Amman have both allowed U.S. planes to patrol no-fly zones over northern and southern Iraq respectively from their own territory.
Ciller's visit was originally scheduled for September but was delayed by the crisis following Baghdad's intervention in northern Iraq in support of a rebel Kurdish faction.

Jordan was one of the few Arab countries not to criticise a proposed Turkish security zone in north Iraq against Turkish Kurd rebels forces in the area. The buffer plan was announced in September but has not yet been put into force.
Turkey angered most Arab states by signing a defence training pact with Israel earlier this year. Jordan, the Arab country with the closest ties to Israel, defended Turkey's decision.
